raidSayLines.line: You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Wei Nair. Hotel housekeeper. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Dispatcher's headset, Field suture kit, Carpenter's square, Mother's Ring, Photo album. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. L
A person, maybe 20s: "We've got days of stores, not weeks. The treeline is the pantry now. Learn what's out there."
📓 Journal: Food won't come to Haven. Walk past the treeline — learn what grows out there, bring it back, and get it named at camp.
Night. The treeline is just a sound now. The fire is the whole argument against it.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.

💬 Yaritza pulls you aside. "I need to tell you something. Last night I... dreamed? No. I was AWAKE. And something spoke to me. Not the System — something else. It said: 'Tell the human to watch the northern treeline.' Then it was gone."
